the study of the psychological characteristics of individuals with eating disorders and the psychological characteristics of their family members.
the personality characteristics of women with eating disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
women who are ill and recovered from eating disorders exhibit personality characteristics that are different than those of normal controls.
the TCI is a promising instrument for assessing personality in women with eating disorder pathology.
the personality characteristics of women ill or recovered from eating disorders are not the same as women without eating or other mental disorder pathology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
personality characteristics may be important to the development and maintenance of eating disorders and may also be important to recovery.

women with eating disorders, in both ill and recovered states, have higher levels of harm-avoidance and lower levels of self-directedness and cooperation than do women without eating disorders, and this is consistent with the literature.
personality characteristics are not simply a result of the eating disorders, but are a risk factor for their development and maintenance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

personality traits, particularly novelty seeking, harm avoidance, and self-directedness, are associated with eating disorders and may be important to consider in treatment planning and in the prevention of eating disorders.
personality characteristics may be a useful marker in predicting the course of eating disorders and that they should be considered in the assessment of eating disorders.
personality characteristics are important in understanding the development and maintenance of eating disorders.
